Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear (not leaf/stalk disease)
- Plump, intact yellow kernels
- Dense white mycelium growing specifically in the inter-kernel crevices/rows
- Some brown discoloration at the tip
- Husks partially pulled back revealing the infection
- No pink/red color (rules out Gibberella), no green (rules out Trichoderma), no olive-green (rules out Aspergillus)

**Candidate comparison:**
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mycelium between kernels, kernels remain intact, matches very well — classic symptom is cottony white growth in crevices with bleached husks
- **Fusarium**: Shows scattered pink/white rot patches, more localized — less consistent with the uniform inter-row pattern seen
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Reference showed brownish/dark husk staining — doesn't match
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**: Green-black mold — doesn't match

The uniform white mycelial growth running between rows of still-intact yellow kernels is the hallmark of Diplodia ear rot.
